value.rationale: Uniform Cayley trees are canonical random-combinatorial objects, and edge indicators are their basic coordinates. The result gives a complete identifiable second-order geometry: a sparse Laplacian covariance becomes a dense positive precision matrix after the fixed-size redundancy is removed. The formulas show that marginally independent disjoint edges acquire substantial negative full-order linear partial correlation.
